\subsection*{p.~113}A mark cited on its own after a space (“marked in the transcription by the diacritic ̭”). In the PDF the mark sits in the space, much as in the NBSP row, so this is not a visible problem; but U+0020 has no anchors in either font, and only an anchored base guarantees the placement: the patch gives NBSP x-height anchors for floating marks (U+25CC dotted circle is the other usual base).\par\smallskip

\subsection*{Checked in context: not font problems}p.~163, example (16), \emph{*̆ḷə ḡawwāyā} `inside': an encoding typo. The PDF has a stray U+0306 after the asterisk (the starred-form marker); the word begins with ḷ, which should not also carry a breve. In print the breve falls on the asterisk and is nearly invisible, but it is in the text. p.~85, (10), \emph{zīyāy, zīyā}: mutool reports the U+0304 of ī in the subset of LibertinusSerif-Regular after an italic i, but the zero-width mark's own outline lands over the i and hides its dot, so it looks right; the bold letters are deliberate. Not a font issue.\par\medskip
